title: Decoder Burst Pacing — reproduce v3 memory jitter and implement telemetry-driven pacing policy
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
A regression was noticed after the flashattn v3 rollout where bursty decoder workloads cause intermittent memory jitter and latency spikes during decode. This ticket is to (1) build a reproducible harness that surfaces the memory-management and kernel-swap behaviour under bursty decodes, (2) add targeted telemetry to pinpoint the precise signals leading to jitter, and (3) implement a telemetry-driven pacing policy to mitigate customer impact while we iterate on kernel/allocator fixes.

Background and motivation:
- Multiple production incidents in the past two weeks show increased decode tail latency and sporadic OOMs during bursty multi-request traffic (mostly short-prefill + long-decode mixes).
- Initial triage points at interaction between v3’s tiling/workspace strategy and our allocator’s shard-level eviction policy: frequent kernel handoffs cause short-lived spikes in device memory allocation churn and temporary workspace thrashing.
- Several customers (enterprise tier) observed degraded latency SLOs when concurrent bursty chats arrived; this is classified as high customer impact.

Observed signals to reproduce locally:
1) Workload shape: 1-4 concurrent requests, each with prefill ~32-64 tokens and decode bursts of 200-800 tokens interleaved with short gaps.
2) Model family: Llama/FA3-like architectures quantized to 4-bit and 8-bit mixes produce stronger effects.
3) Hardware: effect reproducible on H100 and GA100 fleets but more acute on older GPU drivers.
4) Telemetry: increased kernel-switch count, elevated peak cudaMalloc calls, workspace reallocations, decode tail latency > 95th pct baseline by 2.5-3x.

Acceptance criteria:
- Repro harness committed that can deterministically recreate the memory jitter on CI GPUs and a guidance doc on how to run it manually.
- New telemetry added: per-request kernel-switch metric, workspace eviction rate, per-device short-window alloc/dealloc count, and a burst-detection metric emitted to tracing pipeline.
- A lightweight telemetry-driven pacing policy implemented behind a runtime flag that reduces decode emission rate and staggers prefill-to-decode handoffs when burst pattern detected.
- Canary rollout shows drop in kernel-switch spikes and 95th pct decode latency reduced to within 1.2x baseline in the canary cohort.
- Follow-up engineering tasks opened for persistent fixes (allocator tuning, v3 tiling adjustments) with owners assigned.

Planned work and experiments:
- Week 1 (this ticket):
  * Implement harness (simulated clients with synthetic interleaving) and soak-run on CI GPUs (Ethan).
  * Add telemetry hooks in the runtime and exporter (Maya).
  * Hypothesis-run: toggle v2/v3 kernels per-layer to localize which layers/sizes trigger thrash.
- Week 2:
  * Implement pacing PoC: a conservative token-emission throttle that uses a rolling short-window of per-device alloc churn + kernel-switch frequency to decide pacing. Expose as runtime flag and per-tenant override.
  * Run canary with 5% traffic on dedicated pool across GA100/H100. Collect regressions board.
- Parallel: create postmortem artifact and link to customer incident dashboards; coordinate with SRE to open a runbook for manual mitigation.

Mitigation options considered (trade-offs):
- Immediate: telemetry-driven pacing (chosen for this ticket) — low-risk, reversible, reduces throughput but preserves availability.
- Short-term: force fallback to v2 for specific shapes — stable but increases cost and may harm unit economics.
- Long-term: allocator improvements and v3 tiling parameter auto-tuning — higher engineering cost but best for performance; schedule under follow-up tasks.

Artifacts and links:
- Repro harness draft: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tree/feature/decoder-burst-harness (WIP).
- PoC telemetry exporter: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/452 (WIP).
- Design notes and experiment logs: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RT/Decoder+Burst+Pacing+Playbook.
- Customer incident: https://internal.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-034 (masked).

Testing matrix:
- Kernel variants: v2-only, v3-only, per-layer-hybrid.
- Quant modes: fp16, q8_0, q4_1.
- GPUs: H100, A100, GA100.
- Load shapes: steady throughput (baseline), bursty interleaved (target reproduction).

Open questions / blockers:
- Allocator telemetry dimension granularity: current allocator exposes per-shard counts but not per-request attribution. Need to estimate cost of adding per-request tags.
- Can we reuse existing workspace caches to avoid thrash, or does v3 tiling fundamentally force realloc patterns? Need runtime author input (cc @runtime-team).
- Engineering capacity: this ticket overlaps with the ongoing v3 startup shims (ENG-118901). Decide whether to fast-track the pacing flag or fold into that rollout.

Next steps (short-term checklist):
- [x] Create repro harness repository and initial CI job (Ethan, 2026-03-03).
- [x] Add kernel-switch counter telemetry to runtime (Maya, 2026-03-05).
- [ ] Implement pacing PoC and unit tests (Ethan, eta 2026-03-14).
- [ ] Run canary and collect metrics (SRE + Runtime, eta 2026-03-16).
- [ ] If canary passes, create incremental rollout plan and feature flag gating (PM review).

Owners and reviewers:
- Owner: Ethan Patel (runtime performance)
- Telemetry owner: Maya Chen
- Reviewer: Lina Rodriguez (allocator), Priya Nair (runtime lead)
- SRE contact: Jordan Miles

Notes from recent sync (2026-03-11):
- Priya: prioritize telemetry that differentiates kernel-swaps originating from tile size mismatch vs. allocator-induced evictions.
- Lina: adding per-request tags to allocator is feasible but may add 6-8% CPU overhead in hot paths; prefer aggregated short-window attribution initially.
- SRE: will provision canary fleet and add alert thresholds for pacing to auto-ease if latency improves.

Follow-ups (created after this ticket completes):
- ENG-846522: allocator short-window attribution prototype and perf benchmark.
- ENG-846523: v3 tiling autotune experiment and default parameter update.
- ENG-846524: customer communication and postmortem writeup.
